questions.question: An API already has a user's collection and immutable _key and needs one profile. Which ArangoDB access path is the narrowest fit?
options: A two-hop graph traversal
A primary-index key lookup
A full collection scan
An ArangoSearch view
questions.explanation: ArangoDB's key-value model is a subset of its document model, and every collection has a built-in primary index on _key. No relationship or attribute search is required.

questions.question: A catalog query filters by category and active status, sorts by rating, and returns ten documents. What should drive the index design?
options: The full equality-filter and sort shape verified with EXPLAIN
The largest document key in the collection
The number of graph edge collections
A universal index copied from another workload
questions.explanation: A persistent index should match the observed predicates and ordering, then be verified with the actual query plan. Every secondary index also adds write and storage cost.

questions.question: Which attributes make an ArangoDB edge document connect two graph nodes?
options: _key and _rev
source and destination
_from and _to
parentId and childId
questions.explanation: Edges are documents with special _from and _to attributes that reference the source and target document identifiers. Edge collections automatically index these relationship directions.

questions.question: A collection uses tenantId instead of _key as its shard key. What can happen when a lookup supplies only the document _key?
options: The Coordinator may need to contact every shard
The document is always stored on the Agency
The collection automatically changes back to _key sharding
The lookup becomes a graph traversal
questions.explanation: Without the custom shard-key value, the Coordinator may not know the target shard from _key alone. Supplying the shard key as a supported lookup hint can preserve targeted routing.

questions.question: A shard has replicationFactor 3 and writeConcern 2. Both followers are unavailable, but the leader copy remains healthy. What is the expected boundary?
options: All writes succeed because one copy exists
The shard is unreadable, but writes continue
Reads may continue from the surviving copy, but writes requiring two in-sync copies fail
The Coordinator silently lowers writeConcern to 1
questions.explanation: One available replica can preserve read access to that shard, but writeConcern 2 requires two in-sync copies before the configured write acknowledgement can succeed.

questions.question: Which cluster design can provide eligible multi-collection ACID work without crossing arbitrary shard leaders?
options: Adding an unrelated read replica
OneShard with the documented transaction and durability conditions
Using a custom shard key but any number of leader DB-Servers
Sending the same write to two Coordinators
questions.explanation: OneShard places a database's leader shards together so eligible AQL queries and stream transactions can execute within one DB-Server boundary. Arbitrary cross-shard work does not gain one ACID boundary merely because it uses AQL.
